dedupe_keys.name: usgs pedestrian tsunami evacuation time maps for alaska hawaii american samoa the northern mariana islands puerto rico and the us virgin islands

description: This record groups six U.S. Geological Survey data releases that map how long it takes people on foot to leave tsunami hazard zones, made with the USGS Pedestrian Evacuation Analyst Tool (PEAT), an anisotropic path-distance model that weights slope and land cover to find the shortest route from every point in a hazard zone to safety. The 2025 releases by Nathan Wood and Jeff Peters give slow-walk (1.20 metres per second) travel time maps for 20 Alaskan coastal communities facing Aleutian-Alaskan subduction zone scenarios, for Saipan, Tinian and Rota in the Northern Mariana Islands, for 16 tsunami scenarios in Puerto Rico, and for the US Virgin Islands with tables of residents, employees and cruise ship passengers by travel time. The 2018 releases give travel time maps for two hazard zones at three speeds in O'ahu, with resident, employee and hotel visitor exposure, and at four speeds in American Samoa. Coverage: US coasts outside the contiguous states. Access: ScienceBase items with zipped shapefiles, tables and XML metadata, each with a DOI; free. Licence: CC0 1.0 on the 2025 releases; not stated on the 2018 items. Caveats: travel times assume people start at once and ignore congestion and debris; the 2018 items list only metadata files on ScienceBase. Simulation uses are evacuation feasibility, vertical evacuation siting and population exposure inputs for tsunami emergency planning and agent-based evacuation models. Related records: the California probabilistic tsunami hazard zone evacuation times from the same team.
